simple.meaning: כַּרְפַּס (karpaç) is a Hebrew action word meaning “byssus or fine vegetable wool.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Esther, beginning at Esther 1:6. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to כַּרְפַּס (H3768) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: כַּרְפַּס (karpaç) / H3768 is traced through Esther 1:6 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.full: H3768. karpas כַּרְמַּס noun masculine cotton (or fine linen (loan-word from Sanskrit karpâsa , cotton , Persian fine linen ; hence also κάρπασος , carbasus , Arabic Talmud כָּרְמְּסָא ; compare Lag Arm. Stud. § 1148 ); — כ ׳חוּר וּתְכֵלֶת Est 1:6 ( ᵐ5 καρπασίνοις ): compare Cels. Hierob. ii. 157 ff . [ כָּרַר ] verb √ of following (Late Hebrew כִּרְכֵּר use circumlocution ; ᵑ7 . plural כִּרְכְּרָן dances ; Arabic return, repeat, attack anew, advance and retreat ; id. ; II. whirl about ; originally perhaps move around , then surround, enclose, recur , etc.; Ethiopic turn a mill, only participle; see rotate, revolve, roll , and derivatives Di 838f. ); — only Pilpel , Participle מְכַרְכֵּר dancing (literally whirling ) 2Sam 6:14 , 16 (|| מְפַזֵּז ).

occurrences.englishText: There were hangings of white and blue material, fastened with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings and marble pillars. The couches were of gold and silver, on a pavement of red, white, yellow, and black marble.
